texts: good. the habitual living, the cliff-spires as a definite group, the still-going "have always lived" reading and the word "always" are all carried, and the rule fires for any sky-cat.

good. the ledgers become a group, "old" is handed to each ledger by rule, and the Watch attaches as their possessor — worth knowing that a capitalized common noun stays a common noun here, so the Watch is recorded as a thing of kind watch rather than as a name.
good. "the Keepers" is recorded as one named individual and the tolerating of sky-cats attaches to it directly, with no invented group members.
good. it lands as a kind-level claim about sky-cats, "wild animal" is unpacked into animal and wild, and the empirical strength is right for a trait an individual could lack.
